name: Retevis RT3S (OpenGD77)
notes: Retevis RT3S (TYT MD-UV380 family) running OpenGD77 firmware, programmed through qdmr's dmrconf CLI as radio 'openuv380' (detect reports 'Open MD-UV380'). Every limit here is sourced from qdmr v0.15.1 lib/opengd77_limits.cc (OpenGD77Limits, shared by all OpenGD77-family radios via OpenGD77Base::limits()): channels 1-1024 with 1-16 ASCII-char names, zones 0-68 with 80 channels each and 1-16 char names, group lists 0-76 with 1-32 contact refs, DMR contacts 1-1024 with 1-16 char names, and FM/DMR frequency ranges 136-174 and 400-470 MHz (Critical severity). The UHF ceiling is 470, not the MD-UV380 hardware's nominal 480: qdmr rejects above 470 on this radio key, and 470 still covers GMRS (462-467). max_scan_lists is 0 because OpenGD77 has no scan-list entity at all -- scanning is zone-based (hold the zone) -- and qdmr's limits mark scanlists RadioLimitIgnored, so any scan list in a profile would be silently dropped on write; declaring 0 makes codeplugger reject them loudly instead. Other qdmr constraints not expressible in this schema, enforced by 'dmrconf verify --radio=openuv380' in the write path: exactly one DMR radio ID with a name of at most 8 ASCII chars, per-channel power enum limited to Low/High (no Mid step), and DTMF contacts capped at 32. Modes are FM and DMR only; the OpenGD77 limits define no AM channel class, so airband is not representable through this path. Bands and counts deliberately describe the qdmr/OpenGD77 write path, not the TYT OEM firmware: the same hardware under OEM firmware would be a different radio definition. Hardware note (fleet): Eric's eam_rt3s_01 is the STANDARD MD-UV380 board; the 'MD-UV380 (10W Plus)' OpenGD77 build boots with a dead backlight on it. Firmware variant matters for flashing, not for this capabilities file.
